column11: New gate. Reason: the same defect was observed twice on 2026-10-22 - a before/after judgement script read its pre-image with `git show HEAD:path`, so once the change was committed it compared the new revision against itself (carrier-flip card: 721/721 queries identical, changed fields={}; gene-symbol card: the identity judge reported FAIL for the wrong reason). The scanner covers shell- and argv-style calls plus a relative ref hidden in a pre-image constant; references written inside backticks are prose about the hazard and are skipped; any other exemption needs the explicit marker. Scanned surface = pipeline/ mcp_server/ kb/ scripts/ tests/ (build, fixtures and historical docs records excluded).

column7: Stated rule = the gate's own two conditions: the registry on disk equals the source-derived rows AND zero arm pairs on the real tree set a non-cleared switch in one arm only, plus a self-test that catches a planted one-arm switch, accepts a paired one and accepts a harness-cleared one, and rejects a registry drifted by one name
column11: New gate. Reason: a before/after measurement of the recorded set (28 volumes / 721 clusters / 1,495,330 cells) reported `changed = 0` for the carrier flip, which was in fact active. docs/plans/noregr_20261022/scripts/wave_common.py clears a hard-coded SWITCHES tuple written before EYEKB_ACT_ONFIBRO existed, so setting it in the before arm left it set in the after arm and the comparison ran the tree against itself: a silent null produced by the instrument, not by the change. The frozen harness is a delivered artefact and was NOT edited; scripts/switch_coverage/arm_hygiene.py derives the switch list from the source at run time and exposes contaminating(), which implements the arm-pair rule this gate enforces. Scanned surface = every before/after report JSON under docs/plans/.
